notes: GTFOBins abuse-syntax rules. Kibana core fields (id/rule_id/query/tags/...) plus agent-side extension fields (gtfobin/technique/fidelity_notes/benign_scenarios/mitre/abuse_regex). tightened_from_review=true marks rules whose regex was tightened per review verdicts before shipping. process.command_line is the primary field (Convert-LinuxDatasetsToCategoryFiles emits it joined+quoted).

name: [Loaded Potato] GTFOBins awk BEGIN{system(sh)} Shell Handoff
description: awk/gawk/mawk/nawk invoked with a BEGIN block that calls system() with a shell interpreter argument (/bin/sh, /bin/bash, sh -p, etc.). Anchored on the shell target inside system() so admin scripts that shell out to non-shell binaries via awk BEGIN{system("date")} do not fire. Residual FP: security-audit scripts using awk BEGIN{system("/bin/sh ...")} intentionally.
query: process.command_line: ((*awk* OR *gawk* OR *mawk* OR *nawk*) AND *BEGIN* AND *system(* AND (*\/bin\/sh* OR *\/bin\/bash* OR *sh -p*))
author: Loaded Potato
fidelity_notes: awk's role is text stream processing; system() invoking a shell in BEGIN{} uses awk as a shell wrapper (GTFOBins sudo/SUID escape). Tightened per review: system() argument must reference a shell interpreter, not any binary.
benign_scenarios: Security-audit script deliberately spawning /bin/sh via awk BEGIN{system(...)}

name: [Loaded Potato] GTFOBins tar Compress-Program Shell
description: tar's -I / --use-compress-program flag pointed at /bin/sh, /bin/bash, /bin/zsh, etc. The flag exists so tar can call a compressor (gzip, xz, zstd, pigz); pointing it at a shell is only useful for sudo tar command injection.
query: process.command_line: (*tar* AND (*use-compress-program* OR *" -I "*) AND (*\/bin\/sh* OR *\/bin\/bash* OR *\/bin\/dash* OR *\/bin\/zsh*))
author: Loaded Potato
fidelity_notes: Legit compress-program values are pigz/zstd/xz-wrapper. Bare /bin/sh has no legitimate use here. No known benign FPs.

name: [Loaded Potato] nc/ncat/netcat Bind-Shell Listener with -e
description: netcat family in listen mode (-l / -lvnp / --listen) combined with an exec flag (-e / -c / --exec / --sh-exec). Either alone is legitimate (one-shot file receive, or client-side reverse shell already covered by Module 2b); the AND is a bind shell with no benign use.
query: process.command_line: ((*nc* OR *ncat* OR *netcat*) AND (*" -l"* OR *--listen*) AND (*" -e "* OR *" -c "* OR *--exec* OR *--sh-exec*))
author: Loaded Potato
fidelity_notes: Listen mode + exec = bind shell. No benign use case for a netcat listener that auto-execs on connect.

name: [Loaded Potato] python/perl/ruby -c Inline Read of Credential File
description: Interpreter one-liner whose inline code opens /etc/shadow, /etc/gshadow, /etc/sudoers(.d/*), /etc/master.passwd, /etc/security/opasswd, or a private SSH key (~/.ssh/id_*). Production credential access uses spwd/getent APIs, not inline open() against argv paths.
query: process.command_line: ((*python* OR *perl* OR *ruby*) AND *" -"* AND (*\/etc\/shadow* OR *\/etc\/gshadow* OR *\/etc\/sudoers* OR *\/etc\/master.passwd* OR *\/.ssh\/id_*))
author: Loaded Potato
fidelity_notes: Legit scripts open project config files, not authoritative credential stores, via inline -c/-e. Whitelist by parent (auditbeat, security scanner units) if security-audit scripts hit.
benign_scenarios: Security researcher scripting a shadow-file audit inline

name: [Loaded Potato] Shell with -p Privilege-Preservation Flag
description: bash/sh/dash/zsh/ksh started with -p (do-not-drop-privs) — the canonical SUID/sudo shell escape. Combine with user.effective.name=root AND user.name!=root at consumer side for near-zero FP.
query: process.command_line: ((*sh -p* OR *bash -p* OR *dash -p* OR *zsh -p* OR *ksh -p*))
author: Loaded Potato
fidelity_notes: Shells run with real=effective UID by default; -p exists only to preserve euid across SUID boundary. Effectively no benign use.
benign_scenarios: Legacy init.d wrapper explicitly using sh -p (rare, whitelist by exact cmdline)

name: [Loaded Potato] GTFOBins tar --checkpoint-action=exec= Shell
description: tar --checkpoint-action=exec= pointed at a shell interpreter. Tightened per review: exec target must resolve to a shell (/bin/sh, /bin/bash, sh, bash) so backup-progress scripts that use exec=/usr/local/bin/progress.sh do NOT fire.
query: process.command_line: (*tar* AND *checkpoint-action* AND *exec=* AND (*\/bin\/sh* OR *\/bin\/bash* OR *=sh* OR *=bash*))
author: Loaded Potato
fidelity_notes: exec=<shell> under sudo tar is textbook GTFOBins. Non-shell exec targets (backup progress scripts) intentionally excluded by the shell-basename anchor.

name: [Loaded Potato] vim/view/ex -c Shell Escape or Embedded Python
description: vim/nvim/view/ex/vimdiff invoked with -c executing :!<shell> or :py/:python <os.system|pty.spawn|subprocess>. Only automated -c form is caught (bare interactive :! escapes cannot be seen from command_line).
query: process.command_line: ((*vim* OR *view* OR *nvim* OR *vimdiff* OR *" ex "*) AND *" -c "* AND (*:!* OR *os.system* OR *pty.spawn* OR *os.setuid* OR *subprocess*))
author: Loaded Potato
fidelity_notes: -c :!<shell> or -c :py os.setuid is the sudo vim escape. Legit :! use targets fmt/sort/inline-filter, not shells.
benign_scenarios: Editor macro shelling out to a text filter — will not match unless the filter is /bin/sh

name: [Loaded Potato] python -c os.setuid(0) / pty.spawn(shell) / libc.setuid
description: python one-liner calling os.setuid(0)/os.setresuid(0,...), or pty.spawn on a shell binary, or ctypes.CDLL(libc).setuid — GTFOBins python SUID/capabilities escape.
query: process.command_line: ((*python* OR *python3* OR *python2*) AND *" -c "* AND (*os.setuid* OR *os.setresuid* OR *pty.spawn* OR *libc*setuid*))
author: Loaded Potato
fidelity_notes: setuid(0) on a python one-liner has one purpose: elevate/preserve root. Maintenance scripts live in files, not on the command line.
benign_scenarios: Ad-hoc admin one-liner intentionally dropping into a root shell for debugging

name: [Loaded Potato] man -P <shell> Pager Escape
description: man invoked with -P set to a shell binary. -P legitimately picks less/most/more/cat, never a shell.
query: process.command_line: (*man* AND *" -P "* AND (*\/bin\/sh* OR *\/bin\/bash* OR *\/bin\/dash* OR *\/bin\/zsh*))
author: Loaded Potato
fidelity_notes: Zero benign use for shell-as-pager. No tuning needed.

name: [Loaded Potato] systemctl with SYSTEMD_PAGER/PAGER/SYSTEMD_EDITOR=shell
description: Inline env override of SYSTEMD_PAGER/PAGER/SYSTEMD_EDITOR to a shell on a systemctl command line — sudo-systemctl GTFOBins escape.
query: process.command_line: (*systemctl* AND (*SYSTEMD_PAGER=* OR *PAGER=* OR *SYSTEMD_EDITOR=*) AND (*sh* OR *bash*))
author: Loaded Potato
fidelity_notes: systemctl pager defaults to less; overriding to a shell has one purpose. Note: abuse can also happen by exporting the variable in a prior command — rule misses that variant.

name: [Loaded Potato] find -exec <shell> -p / bare shell terminated by \;
description: find -exec/-execdir invoking a shell interpreter that is EITHER given -p (privilege preservation) OR terminated immediately by \; or + with no scripted -c fanout. Eliminates the ubiquitous find ... -exec sh -c '...' _ {} \; benign form (logrotate, dpkg triggers, ansible loops).
query: process.command_line: (*find* AND (*-exec* OR *-execdir*) AND (*\/bin\/sh* OR *\/bin\/bash* OR *\/bin\/dash* OR *\/bin\/zsh*) AND (*" -p"* OR *"\;"* OR *" +"*))
author: Loaded Potato
fidelity_notes: Tightened per review: original rule fired on find -exec sh -c '...' which is the dominant benign form (log gzip fanout, dpkg postinst, ansible file loops). Now requires SUID -p flag OR bare shell with no -c script argument.
benign_scenarios: Rare admin one-liner that opens an interactive bare shell per matched file (very uncommon vs -exec sh -c fanout)

name: [Loaded Potato] socat Listener with EXEC/SYSTEM to Shell or Interactive TTY
description: socat LISTEN endpoint whose EXEC/SYSTEM target is a shell interpreter, OR whose option list carries 2+ interactive-tty flags (pty/setsid/stderr/raw/echo=0/ctty) — the socat reverse/bind shell idiom. Tightened per review: generic EXEC:<binary> for inetd-style relays no longer matches.
query: process.command_line: (*socat* AND (*LISTEN* OR *listen*) AND ((*EXEC:*sh* OR *EXEC:*bash* OR *SYSTEM:*sh*) OR (*pty* AND *setsid*)))
author: Loaded Potato
fidelity_notes: Original rule caught any EXEC/SYSTEM target — matched legitimate git-daemon/nagios/carbon inetd relays. Tightened to require shell target OR ≥2 tty-mode flags.
benign_scenarios: Custom inetd relay that happens to invoke a shell wrapper — very rare

name: [Loaded Potato] python -c socket + connect + dup2 Stdio Hijack (Reverse Shell)
description: python -c payload containing socket.socket AND .connect AND os.dup2 to fd 0/1/2 — the reverse-shell stdio hijack pattern. Tightened per review to require ALL three primitives (original fired on socket+.connect alone, which is every port-probe / wait-for-service one-liner).
query: process.command_line: ((*python* OR *python3*) AND *" -c "* AND *socket.socket* AND *.connect* AND *os.dup2*)
author: Loaded Potato
fidelity_notes: dup2 to stdio has no benign analogue in a python -c one-liner. Combined with socket.socket + .connect it is the textbook reverse-shell payload.

name: [Loaded Potato] ssh -o ProxyCommand=<shell>
description: ssh -o ProxyCommand set to a bare shell (no transport wrapper). Tightened per review: shell must be terminal in the ProxyCommand value; nc-transport wrappers 'sh -c exec nc ... %h %p' no longer match.
query: process.command_line: (*ssh* AND *ProxyCommand* AND (*\/bin\/sh"* OR *\/bin\/bash"* OR *\/bin\/sh "* OR *\/bin\/sh'*))
author: Loaded Potato
fidelity_notes: Tightened per review: original allowed 'sh -c <transport>' which is the ansible ansible_ssh_common_args and OpenSSH manpage bastion pattern.

name: [Loaded Potato] curl/wget Upload of Credential File
description: curl -T / --upload-file, curl -F @<path>, curl --data-binary @<path>, or wget --post-file where the file is /etc/shadow, /etc/passwd, /etc/gshadow, /etc/sudoers, an SSH private key, an auth log, or a cloud/kube/docker credential store. Tightened per review to a sensitive-path allowlist so backup/artifact/CI uploads no longer fire.
query: process.command_line: ((*curl* OR *wget*) AND (*--upload-file* OR *" -T "* OR *--data-binary* OR *" -F "* OR *--post-file*) AND (*\/etc\/shadow* OR *\/etc\/passwd* OR *\/etc\/sudoers* OR *\/.ssh\/id_* OR *\/.aws\/* OR *\/.kube\/*))
author: Loaded Potato
fidelity_notes: Tightened per review: path anchored to authoritative credential stores; backup uploads (nightly.sql.gz to artifactory), Sentry crash uploads, Prometheus pushgateway posts no longer match.
benign_scenarios: Legitimate incident-response upload of /etc/shadow to a forensics bucket — should alert; humans triage

name: [Loaded Potato] authorized_keys Persistence Write
description: tee, install, cp, mv, or >>/>> redirect where ~/.ssh/authorized_keys is the DESTINATION (last token, not source). Tightened per review to require terminal position so 'cp authorized_keys authorized_keys.bak' no longer matches.
query: process.command_line: ((*tee* OR *install* OR *"cp "* OR *"mv "* OR *">>"* OR *" > "*) AND *\/.ssh\/authorized_keys*)
author: Loaded Potato
fidelity_notes: Tightened per review: destination must be a plain authorized_keys path (no .bak/.old suffix, no other trailing tokens). Legit backup renames excluded.
benign_scenarios: Legitimate provisioning tool (cloud-init, ansible) writing an authorized_keys — will match; whitelist by parent

name: [Loaded Potato] cp/mv/install Overwrite of Sensitive System File
description: cp/mv/install where the LAST token is /etc/passwd, /etc/shadow, /etc/sudoers(.d/*), /etc/pam.d/*, /etc/ssh/sshd_config, or authorized_keys. Tightened per review from '\s|$' to '\s*$' so the sensitive path must be the destination, not the source.
query: process.command_line: ((*"cp "* OR *"mv "* OR *install*) AND (*\/etc\/passwd* OR *\/etc\/shadow* OR *\/etc\/sudoers* OR *\/etc\/pam.d* OR *sshd_config* OR *authorized_keys*))
author: Loaded Potato
fidelity_notes: Tightened per review: reads (cp /etc/passwd /tmp/passwd.bak) no longer match — only writes where the sensitive path is destination.
benign_scenarios: visudo-style edit that rewrites /etc/sudoers via a tmpfile+mv — will match; whitelist by parent=visudo

name: [Loaded Potato] curl/wget Stage to /tmp Piped Directly to Shell
description: curl or wget staging to /tmp|/dev/shm|/var/tmp AND the same command_line pipes to a shell OR chmod+x-and-exec follow-up. Tightened per review: bare download-to-/tmp no longer alerts standalone (get-docker.sh installers are ubiquitous).
query: process.command_line: ((*curl* OR *wget*) AND (*\/tmp\/* OR *\/dev\/shm\/* OR *\/var\/tmp\/*) AND (*"| sh"* OR *"| bash"* OR *chmod +x*))
author: Loaded Potato
fidelity_notes: Tightened per review: requires co-occurring pipe-to-shell or chmod+x follow-up on same command line. Bare 'curl -o /tmp/x' does not fire.
benign_scenarios: Docker/Rustup/k3s install one-liners (get.docker.com | sh) — these WILL match and should be triaged; consider whitelist by known-good host at consumer side

name: [Loaded Potato] tar --transform / --xform Extraction Path Traversal
description: tar extract with --transform or --xform rewriting file paths INTO /etc/cron.d/, /etc/sudoers.d/, /root/.ssh/, or /etc/ld.so.preload — cron/sudoers/ssh persistence drop via archive extraction. Tightened per review to --transform/--xform branch only (the -C branch matched routine restores like letsencrypt backups).
query: process.command_line: (*tar* AND (*--transform* OR *--xform*) AND (*\/etc\/cron* OR *\/etc\/sudoers* OR *\/.ssh* OR *ld.so.preload*))
author: Loaded Potato
fidelity_notes: Tightened per review: -C branch dropped (broad FPs on restore-to-subdir workflows). --transform anchor + sensitive-path anchor retained. Separator class widened to include comma (was [@|/], now [@|/,#:]).
benign_scenarios: Package build that legitimately rewrites paths into /etc via tar --transform — rare

name: [Loaded Potato] sudo -u#-1 / --user=#-1 (CVE-2019-14287)
description: CVE-2019-14287 exploit: sudo with a negative UID (-1 or 4294967295) parsed as 0 (root). Tightened per review: removed the '-?' typo that let 'sudo --user=#1' (UID 1) match; now requires explicit '#-1' or '#4294967295'.
query: process.command_line: (*sudo* AND (*"-u#-1"* OR *"-u #-1"* OR *"user=#-1"* OR *"user=#4294967295"*))
author: Loaded Potato
fidelity_notes: Tightened per review: '-?' was optional in original regex, causing 'sudo --user=#1' (UID 1) FPs. Fixed to require the minus or overflow overflow value.

name: [Loaded Potato] apt/apt-get Pre-Invoke Shell Hook
description: apt-get with -o APT::Update::Pre-Invoke or APT::Install::Pre-Invoke pointing at a shell/interpreter payload — sudo apt-get GTFOBins escape. Tightened per review: Post-Invoke/Post-Invoke-Success variants (used legitimately by Dockerfile cleanup) excluded.
query: process.command_line: ((*apt-get* OR *" apt "*) AND *Pre-Invoke* AND (*\/bin\/sh* OR *\/bin\/bash* OR *python* OR *perl* OR *" -c"*))
author: Loaded Potato
fidelity_notes: Tightened per review: Pre-Invoke only (Post-Invoke/Post-Invoke-Success covered legitimate container-image cleanup). Payload must be a shell/interpreter, not any exec.

name: [Loaded Potato] gdb -ex '!'/shell — Shell Handoff (No Python)
description: gdb -ex/-iex passing '!<shell>' or 'shell <cmd>' — GTFOBins gdb sudo/SUID escape. Tightened per review: python/pi/py branches dropped (legitimate coredump pretty-printer loading matched them).
query: process.command_line: (*gdb* AND (*" -ex"* OR *" -iex"*) AND (*"!"* OR *shell*))
author: Loaded Potato
fidelity_notes: Tightened per review: original also matched -ex 'python execfile(...)' which is standard libstdc++ pretty-printer loading. Now anchored on true shell-handoff tokens only.
